title: The Winter Typewriter
premise: In the winter of 1848, in a fictional Central European city on the brink of revolution, Casper Thackeray lives as a woman passing as a man to inherit her late father's typeface-cutting trade. When a census taker, Elias Brandt, notices discrepancies in her papers, he offers silence in exchange for a favor: deliver a sealed letter to a printer now branded an enemy of the state. Casper's deliveries entangle her with the underground press, forcing her to choose between the invisibility she has built her life on and the justice being forged in illegal pamphlets. The armistice that ends the uprising is signed only after Casper testifies — under her true name — about the regime's forged documents, which she alone could authenticate by hand; she loses her shop but gains a public identity, and the novel closes with her cutting a new typeface bearing her own name.
about_author: Gideon Thackeray is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in provincial museums. The Winter Typewriter draws on archives of underground pamphlets and census records discovered during that work.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In the print shop, Casper finishes a commission while concealing her identity from a visiting guild inspector. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine; history feels like something that happens elsewhere.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Census taker Elias Brandt arrives, notices the discrepancy between 'Casper' the son and the shop's records, and leaves without reporting it — but takes a copy of the ledger. Beat: first crack in the armor of invisibility.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Casper's POV. Years earlier, her father promised dying friend and radical printer Anton Voss that his presses would never be silent. Beat: the weight of inherited promises.

chapters.title: The Letter Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Elias returns at night with a sealed letter addressed to Anton Voss, now declared an enemy of the state. He asks nothing aloud, but leaves the letter behind. Beat: complicity begins with silence.

chapters.title: Streets Learning to Burn
chapters.summary: Dual POV (Casper / Elias). Protests erupt; the city splits into barricades and curfews. Casper reads the letter: it names names, including hers. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Underground Compositor
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She finds Anton's hidden press in a cellar chapel and meets his daughter Marta, who distrusts the stranger claiming her father's friendship. Beat: alliance forged through mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Type Remembers
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta tests Casper by asking her to set a page blindfolded; her skill betrays her father's training. Beat: grudging respect, and the first hint that hands reveal what voices hide.

chapters.title: The Forged Decree
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Ordered to help authenticate a government decree justifying mass arrests, Elias recognizes the typeface as cut by Casper's father — stolen from her shop. Beat: horror at how craft becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: Curfew Hours
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Soldiers raid the district; Casper hides Marta's press plates inside a coffin bound for the cemetery. Beat: terror transmuted into dark competence.

chapters.title: Enemy Before the Armistice
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Negotiations for an armistice stall; the regime needs scapegoats, and Anton Voss heads the list. Elias must decide whether to falsify the record that condemns him. Beat: conscience versus career.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Elias offers to destroy the evidence against Voss if Casper disappears with him after the armistice — abandoning Marta and the press. Beat: temptation of safety against loyalty.

chapters.title: Ink in the Snow
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. A courier is caught carrying pamphlets; under torture he gives a partial description that matches Casper. Marta must warn or protect her. Beat: trust tested by survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias smuggles Casper into the government archive to compare the forged decree with her father's original matrices. Beat: revelation — the forgery is cruder than feared, and provable.

chapters.title: A Name Cut in Steel
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. To prove the forgery publicly, Casper must sign an affidavit under her legal name, exposing her concealed identity. Beat: the central choice — invisibility or justice.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Bridge
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A planned handoff of evidence is ambushed; someone informed. Elias is arrested as a traitor to both sides. Beat: collapse of every safe plan.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias endures questioning, refusing to name Casper, while realizing his interrogator already suspects a woman runs the Voss press. Beat: endurance as moral act.

chapters.title: The Cellar Chapel Burns
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Troops torch the cellar chapel; Casper and Marta save the original matrices but lose the press and nearly each other. Beat: grief, and the hardening of purpose.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the armistice tribunal, Casper speaks her full name and demonstrates before the court how the forged decree was cut — by comparing punchwork under magnification. Beat: climax; identity claimed at last.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The forgery unravels the arrests; Voss is freed, Elias is dismissed rather than hanged, and the regime's faction falls. Beat: justice outside the law vindicated, imperfectly.

chapters.title: What Is Owed
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta confronts Casper about the years of concealment and the courier's betrayal — revealed as her own cousin acting to save her. Beat: forgiveness without forgetting.

chapters.title: Empty Shop, Full Drawer
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The guild strips Casper's license; the shop is seized. Packing her father's tools, she finds his letter fulfilling the promise to Voss — written for her to find all along. Beat: mourning turned to inheritance.

chapters.title: A New Face for Old Words
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In spring, in a borrowed room above Marta's rebuilt press, Casper cuts her first original typeface and stamps a trial sheet: her own name, then the word 'witness'. Beat: resolution — power reclaimed as craft, identity as authorship.
